stories.title: Bitcoin climbs back to about $74,000, but a December rate hike now looks almost certain
stories.summary: Bitcoin dipped after Tuesday's hotter-than-expected US inflation report, then recovered to around $74,000 on Wednesday while US stocks rallied harder. Futures markets now price a Fed rate hike in December as near certain, and some traders are betting on a bigger one. Higher rates make safe savings and bonds pay more, which tends to pull money away from risky assets like crypto.
points: October consumer prices rose 0.4% against a 0.3% forecast; core prices (without food and energy) rose 0.3% against 0.2%, per Decrypt.
Bitcoin fell to $72,787 after the report, then recovered to about $74,600 by 12:25pm ET Wednesday, per Bitcoin.com.
CME FedWatch on 10 Nov showed 86.4% odds of a quarter-point December hike, 13.6% for a half-point hike and 0% for no hike, per CryptoSlate.
On the options platform Derive, the odds of bitcoin below $70,000 at Christmas rose to 31% from 15% a week ago; above $80,000 fell to 26% from 53%, per The Block.
About $725M of crypto bets were forcibly closed in 24 hours, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: MSCI decides tonight whether to drop Strategy from its indexes
stories.summary: At about 5pm ET on Wednesday (05:00 Thursday Bangkok), MSCI announces its November index changes under new rules for 'non-operating companies'. Strategy, which holds 850,364 BTC per TheStreet, is a candidate for removal. Funds that copy the index would then have to sell the stock; it would stay listed on Nasdaq.
points: Results come shortly after 11:00pm CET Wed 11 Nov; changes take effect at the close on 30 Nov, per MSCI.
JPMorgan estimated about $2.8B of selling by index funds, and up to $8.8B if other index providers follow; both estimates were made for an earlier version of the rules, per TheStreet.
Funds tracking MSCI hold about 13M Strategy shares, 3.1% of the company, per TheStreet.
Strategy shares closed at $121.07 on 10 Nov, down from $145.16 on 28 Oct, per Bitcoin.com.

stories.title: Money is leaving crypto: fund outflows and the biggest stablecoin shrink since 2022
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin funds had a fourth straight day of net outflows on Tuesday, and the total supply of stablecoins (the digital dollars traders keep ready to buy crypto) shrank by the most since the 2022 bear market. Both point to less fresh money waiting to buy.
points: Tuesday 10 Nov: US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $95M net, the fourth day of outflows in a row, with BlackRock's IBIT down $78M, per SoSoValue data cited by CoinDesk.
Monday 9 Nov: $201.1M left, with IBIT down $213.2M, per TFTC's ETF tracker.
Stablecoin supply fell $14.2B in 30 days, the largest drop since 2022, to just under $280B, per Glassnode data cited by The Block.
Tether's USDT shrank $6.6B over 60 days, per The Block.

briefs.title: OKX and ICE set a 23 Nov launch for tokenized stocks
briefs.summary: Their venture opens a tokenized-securities venue on 23 Nov under the SEC's innovation exemption, with 70 assets confirmed so far from issuers including Coinbase, Circle and Robinhood, per The Block.

briefs.title: Bitcoin heads for a second losing year in a row
briefs.summary: Bitcoin is down about 15.7% in 2026 after falling 6.3% in 2025, which would be its first back-to-back yearly loss, per Decrypt.

briefs.title: Bitmine posts a $6.3B annual loss
briefs.summary: The ether treasury company lost more than $6.3B in the year to 31 Aug as ether fell, per The Block.

briefs.title: Deutsche Bank starts crypto custody
briefs.summary: The bank now holds BTC, ETH, USDC and other tokens for European institutional clients, per The Block.

briefs.title: Prediction market loses in New York court
briefs.summary: A federal judge ruled Novig's sports event contracts are not swaps, so New York gambling law can apply, per The Block.

briefs.title: Bitcoin Core discloses fixed bugs
briefs.summary: Three patched flaws were disclosed, including a high-severity bug that could have stalled mining, per Decrypt.

briefs.title: Kraken adds 200 tokenized European stocks
briefs.summary: Its xStocks offering now has over 1,500 assets; it is not available to US persons, per The Block.

briefs.title: Gram jumps, Zcash slides
briefs.summary: Gram (formerly toncoin) rose about 5% after comments from Telegram's founder, while Zcash fell on forced selling and fund outflows, per CoinDesk.
